Modern.brandNameRationale: Two words. Studio names the practice. Plan names the technical drawing that every project starts with. The brand sits at the moment of decision, before the furniture, before the paint, before the install.
Modern.industrySummary: Modern interior design has moved from one-off residential commissions toward design-led practices with strong portfolios and clear processes. Clients are more design-literate than ever and reward studios that show the work, not just the final shot.
Modern.competitorLandscape: Studio Shamshiri (shamshiri.com) holds the modern design-led peer position. Studio KO (studioko.fr) sits at the international tier. Atelier Vime (ateliervime.com) does the contemporary heritage-leaning middle. We sit closer to Shamshiri in tone.
Modern.positioningStatement: A small interior design studio that shows the plan before the moodboard.

targetAudience.primary: 30 to 55. Homeowners, restaurant founders, gallery owners building something for the first time. Already hired one designer and was unhappy with the surprise costs. Wants the principal in every meeting.

dos: Show the plan and the schedule
Name the principal on every project
donts: Photograph completed rooms with no people

Modern.logoDirection: A wordmark only. STUDIO PLAN in a precise modern grotesk, all caps, two words on one line. A small geometric mark, two thin parallel lines suggesting a floor plan section, used as the favicon and on every page of the project deck.

colorPalette.name: Plan Red

Luxury.brandNameRationale: Two surnames joined by an ampersand. The structure of a heritage interior design practice. Mason and Hart sound like two real partners whose names ended up over the door. The whole name reads as a practice already known to a small set of families.
Luxury.story: Mason & Hart was founded by two principals who had each spent decades inside larger practices and wanted to take fewer clients, more carefully. The studio accepts a limited number of commissions each year. Some clients have been with the firm across multiple homes.
Luxury.industrySummary: Top end interior design has been consolidating into large practices with international offices and quarterly catalogs. There's a parallel market for small, principal-led firms with decades-long client relationships. The customer is paying for the partner, the studio, and the next decade.
Luxury.competitorLandscape: Bunny Williams (bunnywilliams.com) holds the institutional American heritage position. Robert Couturier (robertcouturier.com) sits in the international tier. Studio Sofield (studiosofield.com) does the design-led commercial peer. We sit smaller and quieter than all of them.
Luxury.positioningStatement: A small heritage interior design firm with two principal partners and few clients.

targetAudience.primary: Wealthy. Often inherited. Building or renovating significant residences across multiple cities. Values the partner relationship over the catalog. Books years ahead.

dos: Speak in the language of the craft

Minimal.brandNameRationale: Single word. Room is what an interior designer actually delivers. The brand sits on the unit of the work, not the practice or the philosophy. Plain. Specific. Useful.
Minimal.industrySummary: Most interior design practices have elaborate names, design philosophies, and origin stories. There's an opening for one that strips it all back to the room itself.
Minimal.competitorLandscape: Most studios fail this purity test. The closest spirit is some Japanese interior practices and the no-name aesthetic of certain Scandinavian studios.
Minimal.positioningStatement: An interior design studio that designs rooms. That is the entire offering.

targetAudience.primary: Homeowners who want one room done well. They don't need a five-year design plan. They want this living room or this bedroom fixed.

dos: Show the room before and after

typography.rationale: One face. The proposal, the deliverable, and the invoice all carry the same wordmark.

Corporate.tagline: Workplace design and project delivery at scale.
Corporate.brandNameRationale: Three words. Pinnacle signals top performance. Design Partners closes it as a B2B services relationship. The whole name reads like a real, established workplace design firm already on the procurement panel at corporate real estate teams.
Corporate.industrySummary: Corporate workplace design is a serious B2B category. Companies want partners who can deliver office and workplace projects across multiple sites with operational discipline, budget control, and consistent quality. The category is dominated by giant firms (Gensler, HOK) and a few specialists.
Corporate.competitorLandscape: Gensler (gensler.com) is the global giant. HKS (hksinc.com) holds the institutional peer position. M Moser (mmoser.com) sits in the workplace-design tier. We sit smaller and more focused on the mid-market enterprise client.
Corporate.positioningStatement: Workplace design and project delivery for mid-market enterprise companies.
Corporate.positioningRationale: Mid-market companies are too small for the giant firms' attention and too sophisticated for boutique practices. We sit between them, with operating discipline and modern delivery.

Creative.brandNameRationale: Two words. Good Chair names the smallest unit of a well-designed room. The brand suggests interior design starts with one good object, not a fifty-page proposal. Loud, plain, and slightly self-deprecating.
Creative.manifesto: Most interior design firms sell the full transformation. The cohesive scheme, the curated everything. We made Good Chair because most people don't need a transformation. They need one good chair. One good lamp. One good table. The brand is for the room that gets fixed one piece at a time, by a person who actually lives in it.
Creative.industrySummary: Interior design branding has been polished, magazine-ready, and slightly intimidating. There's room for a practice that's warm, character-driven, sticker-friendly, and serious about helping people improve the rooms they already live in.
Creative.competitorLandscape: Brian Paquette Interiors (brianpaquette.com) does warm-direct well. CB2 (cb2.com) holds the accessible-design middle. Maiden Home (maidenhome.com) sits in the D2C furniture tier. We sit warmer and more honest than any of them.
Creative.positioningStatement: An interior design practice for people who want to fix one room, not redesign their life.
